## Summary

There is a vulnerability in Traefik's request path sanitization. The `sanitizePath` entry point option, enabled by default, resolves the `..` and `.` dot-segments and removes the duplicate slashes from the request path before routing, but it leaves a dot-segment carrying a path parameter, such as `/..;x/`, untouched. Traefik matches its routers and applies its middlewares on this unresolved path and forwards it unchanged. When a backend that strips path parameters (Servlet containers, Spring, ...) is shared between an unauthenticated router and a router protected by an authentication or authorization middleware, an unauthenticated attacker can send a single request such as `/public/..;x/admin` to reach the protected resources and bypass the middleware.

Traefik v2.11.62, v3.7.18 and v3.8.0-rc.2 resolve the `..`, `.` and empty segments carrying path parameters before the dot-segment removal, when `sanitizePath` is enabled (the default). Traefik v3.0 to v3.6 are also affected; these lines are end of life and will not receive a patch, the remedy is to upgrade to a patched release.

## Patches

- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v2.11.62
- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.7.18
- https://github.com/traefik/traefik/releases/tag/v3.8.0-rc.2
